name: Monthly cargo traffic handled at Major Ports
provider: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Government of India
statement: DRAFT — unsigned, binds nothing; registry default_policy: deny governs until the founder signs. Proposed scope: exactly cite_metadata, model_processing and publish_extract, bounded to the two marginal tables of the Monthly Cargo Traffic report at Major Ports — tonnes by Major Port, and tonnes by commodity across all Major Ports — reproduced accurately from the hash-pinned Ministry PDF, each published figure carrying prominent acknowledgement of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, the report month, and the registered extract SHA-256, per the Copyright Policy's accuracy, non-derogatory-use, non-misleading-context and prominent-acknowledgement conditions. NOT approved: redistribute_raw — no re-hosting of Ministry PDFs or page images, matching the registry's own source_bytes_not_redistributed tier (this is IGRM's self-imposed narrowing, not a prohibition in the terms); no port-by-commodity joint cells, which this report does not publish and which no signature here can create; no presentation of these figures as a statement of law or for legal purposes, which the Ministry's Terms & Conditions expressly disclaim; no Ministry endorsement, national emblem or Ministry branding beyond textual attribution; no reproduction of anything inside the report identified as third-party copyright. Also NOT approved: publishing transformed derived series. The Copyright Policy grants accurate reproduction and is silent on adaptation and derivative works, so derived-value publication is outside this scope and needs its own signed decision.

_draft_only.status: UNSIGNED DRAFT - not valid authority until signed
_draft_only.verifier_note: Verified independently at https://shipmin.gov.in/en/footer/copyrightpolicy. The operative grant is "Material featured on this site may be reproduced free of charge in any format or media without requiring specific permission", conditioned on accurate reproduction, non-derogatory/non-misleading use, and prominent acknowledgement where published to others. publish_extract of the two marginal tables sits squarely inside that reproduction grant, and the draft carries all four conditions explicitly into scope. cite_metadata is a fortiori. model_processing is covered by "in any format or media" (machine copy/extraction) and does not reach adaptation, because the draft withholds publication of transformed derived series — correct, since the policy contains no adaptation or derivative-works language. The policy's single carve-out ("material ... identified as being the copyright of a third party") is honoured as an express exclusion rather than assumed away. I checked the third-party risk directly: the access_url page renders the report as a Ministry publication with the PDF hosted on the Ministry's own domain at shipmin.gov.in/sites/default/files/Report%20Monthly%20Major%20Port%20February%
_draft_only.unresolved_for_founder: Four things to check personally before signing. (1) The Copyright Policy's only carve-out is material "identified as being the copyright of a third party". I read the policy page, not every page of the February 2026 PDF — confirm no page of the report bears a third-party copyright mark, or scope the approval to the two extracted tables only. (2) The terms are on their face broader than this draft: "reproduced free of charge in any format or media" would support redistribute_raw. I excluded it to match the registry's source_bytes_not_redistributed tier. If you want raw re-hosting, that is a widening you can make deliberately — this draft is not evidence that the terms forbid it. (3) This draft does NOT cover publishing transformed derived series, which the existing packet at governance/decisions/DRAFT_india_major_ports_pdmp2.md requests as derive_published_aggregates. The Ministry text is a reproduction permission with no adaptation language, so I could not grant it. Decide whether you want it, and on what reading. (4) max_current_age_days: 62 is a proposed operational bound (two monthly publication cycles, one missed month tolerated), NOT anything the terms supply — the registry currently holds null. Reset it to whatever cadence the pipeline actually needs. Also note, across all three drafts: the live registry vocabulary (cite_metadata / model_processing / publish_extract / publish_derived_value) differs from the proposed vocabulary in governance/decisions/README.md (retain_committed_extract / derive_published_aggregates / quote_attributed_figures / redistribute_in_audit_bundle / redistribute_raw). These drafts use the live registry vocabulary; the existing DRAFT_*.md packets use the README's. Reconcile the two before signing anything, or the signed artifact and the packet will not mean the same thing.
